title: The MCP-native stack
summary: The stack picked for agent surfaces: code hosting, chat, tracker, wiki, CRM, errors, and analytics — at nearly every judged step the top vendor ships an official MCP server, so the agents that run your company can actually reach it.

parts.title: Set up a code hosting org
parts.guidance: Create the code-hosting organization around company ownership, maintainers and repository access requirements. Use the code-hosting workflow to test contributor and automation permissions before moving active work. Verify any intended agent integration against the selected product's actual tools and scopes, recording supported operations, permission scopes and the handoff for unavailable actions.

parts.title: Set up team chat
parts.guidance: Set up team communication around actual working groups, announcement needs and access boundaries. Configure the chat workflow and test member onboarding before adding integrations. For agent participation, verify the specific connection and permissions available in the chosen workspace, documenting where a human must still approve messages or access to private conversations.

parts.title: Set up a project tracker
parts.guidance: Set up work types, stages, ownership and completion criteria in the tracker. Create and move a representative item to check assignments and history. Verify the actual agent connector's supported operations and permissions, recording a manual handoff for missing actions so the team's workflow does not depend on an assumed integration capability.

parts.title: Set up a team wiki
parts.guidance: Organize the wiki around the information people and agents need to find, with clear document owners and access boundaries. Check that a reader can find current instructions and distinguish them from drafts or superseded pages. Test the intended agent connection against those same documents, recording which pages and operations the connection can reach and the manual handoff for the rest.

parts.title: Set up a CRM
parts.guidance: Set up CRM records, stages and ownership for the company's sales process, with customer data access limited appropriately. Validate a representative contact and opportunity through the CRM workflow. Check which reads and mutations the chosen agent connection actually supports, and require scoped authorization before external outreach or consequential changes to customer records.

parts.title: Set up error tracking
parts.guidance: Add error monitoring to the systems the team will operate, with useful context, privacy filtering and clear triage ownership. Follow the monitoring workflow to trigger a controlled error and verify routing. Check the agent-facing tool's diagnostic access and data filtering, then connect findings to the team's triage and release process.

parts.title: Set up product analytics
parts.guidance: Define the product events and questions that the analytics system should support before connecting agent access. Implement and validate the measurement plan through the analytics workflow. Verify the selected integration's actual query and permission scope, then compare an agent-produced result with a known event sample to check the data and access assumptions behind the analysis.
